hero.title: The Three Jewels of Buddhism
hero.description: An exploration of the Triratna—Buddha, Dhamma, and Sangha—which form the foundational pillars of Buddhist ethics and spiritual practice.

sections.title: 1. Core Study Notes
sections.content:
Core Components

  • Buddha: The enlightened teacher, the guide.
  • Dhamma: The doctrine of the Middle Path (Madhyamapratipada).
  • Sangha: The monastic community of monks and nuns.

Philosophical Pillars

  • Four Noble Truths: Dukkha, Samudaya, Nirodha, Magga.
  • Eightfold Path: The practical application of Dhamma.
  • Evolutionary Mindmap:
    • Sermon at Sarnath: Origin of Triratna.
    • Vinaya Pitaka: Rules governing the Sangha.
    • Sutta Pitaka: Contains the exposition of Dhamma.
JewelSignificance
BuddhaAttainment of Bodhi
DhammaEnd of Dukkha
SanghaPreservation of Tradition

timeline.title: The Chronological Framework
timeline.description: Key stages in the evolution of the Triratna from inception to institutionalization.

cards.details: Gautama Buddha attains enlightenment and formalizes the concept of the Three Refuges (Tisarana) after his first sermon.
Ashoka the Great patronizes the Sangha, cementing the Three Jewels as the standard state-supported religious doctrine.

mnemonics.title: Mnemonics & Tricks to Remember
mnemonics.description: Essential memory aids for UPSC Prelims.

items.title: B.D.S.
items.decryption: Remember the hierarchy of refuge: The Teacher (Buddha), the Teaching (Dhamma), and the Community (Sangha).

items: Do not confuse Buddhist Triratna (Buddha, Dhamma, Sangha) with Jain Triratna (Right Faith, Right Knowledge, Right Conduct).
Remember that 'Dhamma' in Buddhism refers to the cosmic law/teaching, whereas Ashoka's 'Dhamma' was a socio-ethical code.
